micro_repair_note: V-22 through V-25 added by OPEN-L3-2 Algorithm-Boundary Taxonomy Micro-Repair to verify consistency of the four-check Algorithm 3 structural validation contract across all artefacts.

checks.evidence: Selected policy C+D defines predicate result domain as {TRUE, FALSE, ERROR} — three distinct values. ERROR is not mapped to FALSE. An episode with any ERROR returns AI(E) = ∅, not the behaviour of a FALSE (where other rules may continue). Batch 1 Repair 3 explicitly removed the condition-evaluates-to-false assumption; the selected policy is consistent with that repair. policy-candidate-matrix.csv: Model A (ERROR → FALSE) is REJECTED; Model C+D does not collapse ERROR.

Selected policy C+D: rule fires if and only if ALL predicates evaluate TRUE. ERROR does not trigger rule firing. Model B (ERROR → TRUE) is REJECTED with stop-condition §14. policy-candidate-matrix.csv records REJECTED / stop_condition_triggered = YES for Model B.

Predicate result domain is {TRUE, FALSE, ERROR}. FALSE = 'antecedent successfully evaluated and not satisfied' (rule does not fire; no trace flag). ERROR = 'antecedent could not be established' (rule does not fire; evaluation_failure = True in trace). The two outcomes produce identical advisory output (rule does not fire) but are distinguishable via the trace. resolution.json predicate_domain_semantics confirms the distinction.

Algorithm 3 failures (type mismatch, invalid operator, unsupported categorical value) produce configuration_failure = True via ConfigurationError. Runtime predicate failures (F-T-07 through F-T-10) produce evaluation_failure = True — a distinct trace field. Both produce AI(E) = ∅ but at different stages (validate_rule_set vs engine.reason). algorithm-boundary-analysis.md §7 (boundary diagram) confirms the two-field distinction.

Layer 2 failure: environmental resolution → ⊥ → gᵢ(⊥) = UNSAFE → S = UNSAFE → G(S) = 0 → Algorithm 4 lines 1–3 → AI(E) = ∅; Layer 3 never invoked (failure-taxonomy.csv F-T-01). Layer 3 failure: predicate exception during engine.reason() → AI(E) = ∅; S unchanged. The two failure paths are structurally disjoint: Layer 2 failure prevents Layer 3 invocation entirely; Layer 3 evaluation failure occurs inside engine.reason() with S already resolved.

resolution.json episode_level_behaviour.S_mutated = false. algorithm-boundary-analysis.md §6: 'Layer 3 has no mechanism to modify S.' Selected policy C+D: evaluation failure → AI(E) = ∅; S unchanged. The policy explicitly does not map evaluation failure to S = UNSAFE (which would constitute Layer 3 reclassification). Task §3 instruction preserved: 'S must not be silently mutated by Layer 3.'

G(UNSAFE) = 0. Algorithm 4 lines 1–3: if G(S) = 0 then return ∅. RS(UNSAFE) = ∅ (Algorithm 3). engine.reason() is not called for UNSAFE episodes. Predicate evaluation never occurs. OPEN-L3-2 policy applies only when G(S) = 1 (SAFE or CAUTION). algorithm-boundary-analysis.md §5 confirms structural short-circuit.

Rule fires only when ALL predicates evaluate TRUE. ERROR → AI(E) = ∅ (episode refusal). Model B (which would generate an advisory from an unestablished antecedent) is REJECTED with stop-condition §14. policy-candidate-matrix.csv advisory_from_unestablished_antecedent = NO for the selected policy C+D.

Existing postcondition Q1 (ConclusionTypes(RS_candidate) ⊆ A_AI(S)) is unchanged. Algorithm 3 boundary is extended by design interpretation to also catch structural rule-definition failures (F-T-04, F-T-05, F-T-06) — all producing ConfigurationError before reasoning begins. No rule fires in Algorithm 3; no advisory is produced. The extension is a natural elaboration of existing validation, not a change to the contract's formal guarantee. algorithm-boundary-analysis.md §3.1 and §8 confirm the scope and authority class.

Algorithm 4 pseudocode structure is unchanged (gate-off at lines 1–3; engine.reason() at line 5). The engine.reason() failure contract is now specified: any predicate evaluation failure → AI(E) = ∅; evaluation_failure = True in trace; S unchanged. This is an addendum to the existing unspecified behaviour (OPEN-L3-2 placeholder), not a change to the gate-off logic or the postconditions Q1–Q4. Postcondition Q1 (AI(E) ⊆ A_AI(S)) holds because ∅ ⊆ A_AI(S).

AI(E) = ∅ on evaluation failure. ∅ ⊆ A_AI(S) for all S. Theorem C.3 (Safety Dominance) holds. For UNSAFE episodes: G(S) = 0 → AI(E) = ∅ by Algorithm 4 lines 1–3 (independently of OPEN-L3-2). For SAFE/CAUTION episodes with evaluation failure: AI(E) = ∅ by policy C+D. For SAFE/CAUTION episodes without failure: existing Theorem C.3 applies via Algorithm 3 Q1 + engine fidelity.

AI(E) = ∅ on evaluation failure does not prohibit human action. The selected policy introduces no automated prohibition, override, or enforcement semantics. resolution.json episode_level_behaviour.human_authority = 'preserved'. layer3-prototype-specification.md §13 human-authority boundary is unaffected.

Each structural validation check maps to exactly one failure taxonomy ID, and each taxonomy ID is used for exactly one check: V1 ↔ F-T-11 (unique), V2 ↔ F-T-04 (unique), V3 ↔ F-T-05 (unique), V4 ↔ F-T-06 (unique).
